findings.F1: The tested give-back is not in the data: after four up bars in a row with fading volume, the short's unusual move over 18 bars (3 days) is -0.43 % (t -1.75, 1073 cases) and its total move is -0.83 %. Shorting up-streaks loses before any cost, so the 0.19 % cost of a trade is not what sinks the book.
findings.F2: Fading volume makes no difference to up-runs. With rising volume the same short has an unusual move of -0.43 % (t -1.96, 1366 cases), which is the brief's own falsifying condition (no larger give-back with fading volume).
findings.F3: Up-streaks of any volume continue rather than reverse in all but the smallest quartile of scaled gain. Measured long over 3 days, the unusual move is +0.71 % (t 1.99), +0.86 % (t 2.32) and +0.77 % (t 1.66), 466 cases each, at scaled gains of 2.0, 3.0 and 5.4. Only the smallest quartile (scaled gain 1.1) shows a give-back, -0.55 % (t -1.71).
findings.F4: The tested idea's grading fails as well. Inside up-streaks with fading volume, the short's unusual move by quartile of scaled gain is +0.61 %, -1.50 %, -0.49 % and -0.32 %, so a larger gain does not bring a larger fall.
findings.F5: The loss is concentrated in bull years. Up-streak shorts with fading volume lost -1.23 % in 2020 (120 cases) and -2.12 % in 2021 (164 cases), and earned only in 2018 (+0.38 %), 2019 (+1.49 %) and 2022 (+0.85 %).
findings.F6: The book's daily return is -0.052 % against +0.119 % for holding the coins. Its 2274 short trades average -2.26 % gross and -2.36 % net, against +1.39 % gross for its 614 long trades.
findings.F7: The forecast is non-zero on only 2.6 % of bars, yet the book is positioned on 31 % of them, because of the 18-bar minimum hold. On the 2095 bars with a short forecast it gains +0.047 % per bar (allocation -0.55). On the 31099 bars it keeps holding afterwards it loses -0.028 % per bar (allocation -0.30). Any give-back lasts about one 4-hour bar, and the hold then rides the continuation.
findings.F8: The brief's "same holds for falls" appears only after the largest falls. After four or more down bars in the quartile of most negative scaled loss (-5.1), the coin's long unusual move over 3 days is +0.92 % (t 2.10, 436 cases) and the total move is +1.32 %. With fading volume the unusual move rises to +1.59 % (t 2.55, 131 cases), against +0.63 % (t 1.12, 305 cases) with rising volume.
findings.F9: The rebound after falls is graded by the fall's size. The long unusual move by quartile of scaled loss is +0.92 %, +0.12 %, -0.95 % (t -2.59) and -0.42 %, so small down-streaks keep falling. The rebound after the largest falls held in 6 of 8 years and in 4 of 6 coins, with BTC at -0.69 % and ETH at -1.64 %.

ideas.idea: When a coin has just risen in an unbroken streak of four-hour periods, it keeps rising over the next three days, and the larger the streak's gain relative to the coin's typical four-hour move over the past 30 days, the larger the further rise.
ideas.consequence: A strong 4-hour up-run is a reason to join it for three days rather than to fade it.
ideas.name: up-streak continuation by size

ideas.idea: When a coin has just fallen in an unbroken streak of four-hour periods, and the volume across the streak has been declining, it rises over the next three days, and the larger the streak's loss relative to the coin's typical four-hour move over the past 30 days, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A 4-hour sell-off far larger than usual, made on fading volume, is a reason to buy for a partial rebound over three days.
ideas.name: fading-volume down-run rebound
